title: Uncle Dewey Schmid and the old vaudeville and cabaret pianists
summary: His uncle was a vaudeville entertainer who worked with old piano players on Rampart Street and encouraged his playing.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: What was your uncle's name then?

My uncle's name was Dewey Schmid. He's at present District Fire Chief of the city. But he also went with the name of Wilbur Leroy. He used to be with the old-time Waterville comedians, Eddie Chittenden and Ralph Nugas and Paul Soipass. They played the old No Name Theater and all the old theaters and the old days. So, he's still around.
He'd be a good person who likes to see, wouldn't he?

My uncle would be very good because he was associated with quite a good number of these old musicians, especially these old piano players that used to play down on, let's see, I believe it was the, on Ramport Street there. It was an old cabaret called, oh, I just can't remember the name of it right now. Was it near Tom Anderson's?
Yeah, it was around there somewhere.

In fact, I think it might have been one of Tom, might have been Tom Anderson's. Because in those days, he worked around those places singing, you know, working with these old piano players. You know, he knew quite a good bit of them. Some called the name of Martinez, the old piano player. And he worked with Buzzy Williams. You know, he worked with quite a number of them. Did you know Martinez? No, I don't believe I did. It seems as though there was a Martinez in the union, an old timer.
And I just don't recall his first name right now. But I know that he played down there.

I don't know if he played on Basin Street, but I know he played at this old club on Ramport. I've heard of him. And of course, naturally, my uncle, Dui Schmid, was quite instrumental in giving me a lot of encouragement. And of course, he was a man of the union. And he was a man of the union, an old timer. And I just don't recall his first name right now. But I know that he played down there. I don't know if he played on Basin Street, but I know he played at this old club on Ramport. I've heard of him. And of course, naturally, my uncle, Dui Schmid, was quite instrumental in giving me a lot of encouragement of playing piano. Because you love that old style of playing.
